notes:
Account overview: Mid-stage payments platform, heavy real-time authorization and post-transaction risk scoring. Interested in replacing current endpoint-hosting + ad-hoc GPU infra with a predictable reserved capacity model. Primary ask: dedicated capacity sizing workshop to validate baseline QPS -> reserved GPU recommendation and SLA language for deterministic latency.

Key stakeholders: CTO (Aaron Holt), Head of ML Ops (Priya Nair), Payments SRE (Marco Ruiz), Procurement (K. Bell). AE: Maya Chen; SE: Daniel Park.

Workload summary (from scoping call 2026-02-18):
- Workloads: real-time chat for payments support (human-in-the-loop + assistant), fraud-reranking pipeline (rerank top-n candidate transactions per second), semantic embeddings for transaction search/alerts.
- Baseline steady-state: 180 QPS across primary region (NA), median request size ~120 tokens, 95th token length ~420 tokens.
- Peak: 900 QPS sustained for 10-15 minutes during batch settlement windows and flash traffic events; observed 3x daily micro-peaks.
- Target latency SLOs: chat p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 280ms; reranking end-to-end p95 <= 350ms. Strong preference for P50/P95 measured at application edge.
- Throughput goals: token/sec baseline ~21,600 tokens/sec (180 QPS * 120 tokens); peak token/sec up to ~378,000 tokens/sec during bursts (900 QPS * 420 tokens).

Workshop goals (requested):
- Validate baseline QPS vs request size distribution and map to model variants (e.g., Llama-2-Chat-70B q4 -> candidate, plus quantized 13B variants for fallback).
- Sizing exercise: reserved GPU counts for steady-state + burst headroom, autoscale granularity, predicted token-per-second capacity per GPU with Redwood kernels.
- SLA negotiation prep: define guaranteed throughput (tokens/sec) per reserved unit, clear latency SLOs with measurement method, credits/penalties for incidents and fallback behaviors.
- Cost modeling: show unit economics (token cost) for batching/kv-cache configurations and tradeoffs for lower-cost fallback models during overload.
- Disaster/fallback playbook: routing policies across dedicated/pinned models, region fallback, and temporary degrade modes (reduced top-k, condensed prompts).

Recent timeline / touches:
- 2026-02-12: Intro demo with hosted API (proof-of-concept flow). Gmail thread + demo video posted.
- 2026-02-18: Scoping call + initial traffic profile collected (Fireflies ff_20260218_timbersize_meeting). Action: AE requested logs and 7-day tail latency histogram.
- 2026-02-24: SE reviewed payload samples; suggested 2 model variants for canary (13B quantized + 70B int8).
- 2026-03-01: Procurement asked for a draft SLA template and estimated reserved GPU monthly cost.
- 2026-03-05: Internal legal submitted data residency requirements (EU region for EU customers; NA for domestic).

POC / evaluation plan proposed by Redwood SE (Daniel):
- Week 0: 1-day onsite sizing workshop with ML/Ops + SRE to walk traffic matrix and confirm QPS/token distributions. Deliverable: sizing spreadsheet and recommended reserved GPU configuration (steady vs burst).
- Week 1-2: 2-week canary on Redwood Dedicated (small reserved cluster) running production traffic slice (5-10% traffic). Metrics: p50/p95 latency, token/sec, cost per million tokens, cache hit-rate, tail latencies under burst.
- Post-canary: SLA redline session with Legal + Ops to lock in uptime/latency credits, capacity guarantees and failover commitments.

Key negotiation points to prepare for SLA session:
- Define measurable SLOs using application-edge timing (ingest -> final token). Need to align on instrumentation and reporting cadence.
- Throughput guarantees per reserved GPU in tokens/sec and QPS equivalents; request ability to burst beyond reserved for limited minutes with defined overage rates.
- Penalty/credit framework: tiered credits for missed p95 latency and for availability loss > 2 hours.
- Data residency and egress commitments for transaction data; integration with their KMS for key separation.

Quotes / customer language captured on call:
- "We need deterministic tails — a few 95th-percentile spikes cost us chargebacks and manual review overhead." — Priya Nair (Head of MLOps).
- "If you can quantify reserved GPU needed for our peak windows and guarantee latency, procurement will be able to accelerate." — K. Bell (Procurement).

Open items / asks from Timberline to Redwood:
- SE: run synthetic load test with customer's payload distribution using recommended kernels; provide per-GPU tokens/sec and estimated number of GPUs for 180 QPS steady + 900 QPS peak.
- AE: produce draft Dedicated pricing (monthly reserved + burst) and sample SLA redline.
- Legal: confirm support for EU data residency + KMS integration.
- SRE/OPS: confirm network topologies for VPC peering and egress constraints.

Next steps (short):
1) Schedule 1-day sizing workshop (onsite) in week of 2026-03-22.
2) Redwood SE to deliver synthetic-run results and spreadsheet by 2026-03-19.
3) Procurement to review draft SLA and respond with must-have clauses by 2026-04-02.

CRM shorthand / internal notes:
- Priority: high. Enterprise logo, rapid ramp potential into Dedicated annual commit.
- Risk: legal wants stronger residency + indemnity. Procurement price sensitivity but willing to commit if SLOs firm.
- Recommended play: accelerate onsite sizing workshop + follow immediately with canary reservation to prove SLOs before procurement sign-off.
